beginner.summary: For Python developers, data engineers and ML engineers who need fast similarity search over embeddings and have not used Meta's FAISS library before. Covers installing faiss-cpu, the float32 array contract, exact search with IndexFlatL2 and IndexFlatIP, squared L2 versus inner product and cosine, reading search results, ID mapping with IndexIDMap, persistence with write_index and read_index, k-means clustering, first IVF, HNSW, scalar quantization and product quantization indexes, index_factory strings, measuring recall against brute-force ground truth, removal and filtered search with IDSelector, range search, keeping metadata next to an index, and a semantic document search capstone.
prerequisites: Writes Python 3 scripts comfortably, including functions, virtual environments and pip installs
Uses NumPy arrays: shapes, dtypes, slicing and np.random for test data
Understands at a high level what a text or image embedding is and why nearby vectors mean similar items
outcomes: Install FAISS, build exact and approximate indexes and run k-nearest-neighbour searches on float32 NumPy data
Choose between squared L2, inner product and cosine similarity and prepare vectors correctly for each
Build IVF, HNSW, SQ and PQ indexes directly and through index_factory, then measure their recall@k against exact search
Persist an index with its own IDs and a metadata store, and serve semantic search over a real document collection
